title.narrative: Contribution to the Green Climate Fund (GCF)

description.narrative: The GCF was established under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change as the central mechanism for climate action. As the largest and highest profile climate fund, it is seen as a marker of international credibility on climate finance. As the world’s largest climate fund, GCF accelerates transformative climate action in developing countries through a country-owned partnership approach and use of flexible financing solutions and climate investment expertise. By re-engaging we want to ensure climate finance works for those who are the most vulnerable to climate change, including for Pacific island countries.

participating-org.narrative: AUSTRALIA - Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade

organisation.narrative: Australia - Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade

title.narrative: Climate adaptation, mitigation, environment and biodiversity

description.narrative: Through the world’s largest global climate fund, the Green Climate Fund (GCF), Australia is enhancing access to climate finance for small island developing states and least developed countries, given their unique vulnerability to climate change impact. In particular, Australia advocates for GCF funding that meets the needs of our Pacific partners, recognising climate change is the single greatest threat to their livelihoods, security, and well-being. We are seeing positive results, including greater GCF project funding and accredited entities in the Pacific along with steps towards a GCF regional presence in the Pacific. DFAT funding towards GCF funded activities is estimated to have strengthened 46,875 peoples’ resilience to climate change and disasters through protective infrastructure, early warning systems, and capacity-building.
